projects.description:

Its objective is to reduce the impact of climate change and increase the resilience of the affected population in the semiarid region of Northeastern Brazil. projects.name: IFAD - 2000002694 – Piauí inclusive sustainable rural development achieved (Piauí Inclusive and  Sustainable Project PSI)
projects.description:
The Piauí Inclusive and  Sustainable Project is a collaboration between IFAD, IDB and the state of Piauí and seeks to promote sustainable rural development in the Piauí-Canindé basins in the semiarid region of Piauí with a focus on the interconnected problems of water scarcity, environmental degradation, lack of sanitation in rural communities, low agricultural productivity, and vulnerability of production systems to climate change facing small-scale farmers and vulnerable populations. The overall Project objective is to improve income, food security, access to basic services, and adaptation to climate change of the rural population living in the semiarid region of Piauí. The specific objectives are: (i) improve access to water for domestic use and production; (ii) improve the environmental conditions of rural families and their surroundings; and (iii) increase the adoption of agricultural technologies, with emphasis on climate change adaptation and mitigation, and the integration of small-scale producers, especially women, youth and Afro-descendants, into value chains.

PSI will directly benefit 60,000 families (about 210,000 people), of which 50% will be women-led and 20% youth-led, and at least 4,800 families from traditional communities. Some 31,000 families will benefit from group-based investments and TA to improve production and marketing, 28,000 will benefit from access to water and 6,500 from sanitation. In order to be aligned with IFAD portfolio in Brazil and IDB requirements the PSI will target families. The Project area will cover 138 municipalities. Its geographic targeting strategy is based on the state priority for water investments in the watershed of the Piauí and Canindé rivers in Piauí’s semiarid region, and selects areas with high levels of poverty and vulnerability to climate change, food and nutrition insecurity, and a low human development index (HDI). The target population comprises poor family farmers and poor rural populations, with priority to women, youth and traditional communities, from rural communities facing lower HDI, lack of water and sanitation services, greater limitations in agricultural productivity, less access to TA services, and environmental degradation processes.

Actual Start Date: 28/11/2023
Actual End Date: 31/12/2029

IDB loan: US$ 100 million
State government counterpart: US$ 29.5 million

projects.name: IFAD - 2000002987 (UNDP)– Amazon Sustainable Management achieved (Amazon Sustainable Management Project PAGES)
projects.description:
PAGES’ goal is to contribute to reducing rural poverty while decreasing deforestation and environmental degradation in the Amazon region of Maranhão. Its development objective is to improve the livelihoods and the food and nutrition security of the rural poor through the conservation and sustainable use of the Amazon rainforest. Through the intervention, the project will increase the resilience of 64,000 people and reduce approximately 6 million tons of CO2 equivalent. The intervention area comprises three development regions in the state: Maranhense Amazon, Maranhense Gurupi, and Pindaré. The target group includes 20,000 organized family farms facing poverty and associated with rural organizations (approximately 80,000 people), at least 12,5% of which are from 2,500 indigenous and other traditional communities (about 1,200 indigenous families, 800 quilombolas, and 500 coconut breakers), 50% women and 25% young people.

projects.name: UNEP Realizing the Biodiversity Conservation Potential of Private Lands
projects.description:
Half of the remaining natural vegetation cover in the five Brazilian biomes this project focuses on (Atlantic Forest, Cerrado, Caatinga, Pantanal and Pampa), amounting to 88 million hectares of natural vegetation, are located on private lands. Although a massive investment is underway to georeference these areas, with almost 70% national coverage completed, their ability to contribute to biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services provision, which is underpinned by their sustainable landscape and forest management is hindered by a lack of i) management guidelines for landscape 
stakeholders; ii) Incomplete Federal regulations on management regimes allowed on these private set-aside areas; iii) the inexistence of tools for the public sector to conduct strategic planning and management of these set-aside areas at macroscales; and iv) appropriate incentives mechanisms to influence private land-owners in priority areas to adopt practices that would improve biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services provision. This project, that has both pilot and macro policy level elements, aims to address these barriers by a)providing these missing elements, b)by piloting them on-the-ground in two Key Biodiversity Areas (KBA) (approx. 1 mi hectares) and c)via a sectorial agreement with the forestry sector to improve the management of their private set-aside areas. A successful implementation will have a direct contribution of conserving over 50 endangered species, scaling-up sustainable landscape management and appropriate systems of sustainable forest management in millions of hectares of Private Set-Aside Areas (PSAA). More importantly, it will create the basis of a national management system of conservation and management for 88 million hectares of PSAA and their wider landscapes.

projects.name: FAO GCP/BRA/085/GFF Desertification Process in Susceptible Areas of Brazil Reversed: Sustainable Agroforestry Practices and Biodiversity Conservation implemented
projects.description:
The project objective is to halt and reverse environmental degradation in areas susceptible to desertification (ASD), ensuring the flow of ecosystem services, promoting the integrated management of natural resources, generating environmental benefits and contributing to poverty reduction.
Outcome 1.1: INRM has been mainstreamed and scaled up at landscape level.
The targeted project value for this outcome is 904,142 ha., No baseline exists. Assessment of the practices and experiences of the production systems and across market value chain (in the project area will be undertaken at the onset of the project using appropriate assessment tools with local experts).  The project will result in 20% increase in purchase of NTFPs by institutional markets and technical guidance for state environmental agencies. Guidelines will be developed for identification and evaluation of INRM systems, and 100 technical staff trained and prepared to use the guidelines and conduct the assessment.
Outcome 2.1: Forest areas under multi-purpose Sustainable Forest Management (SFM) have been increased. 
The targeted project value for this outcome is 15,000 ha under multiple-use forest management, starting from 1,712 ha in the project area.  
Outcome 3.1: Seed/seedling production capacity improved to support restoration of degraded lands in ASD.
The targeted project value for this outcome is an increase by 20% of nurseries production improved and registered (legal), as well as capacity developed on seed and seedling production good practices and registrations standards for 1600 personnel of the tree nursery network. 
Outcome 3.2: Forest connectivity sites have been defined, sustainably managed and restored.
The targeted project values for this outcome are 30,000 ha of new forest connectivity through restoration of degraded land, innovative and appropriate forest regeneration, enrichment and planting techniques.
Outcome 4.1: Improvement in capacity of key state and municipal institutions about LD and desertification.
The targeted project value for this outcome is increased capacity and knowledge of the 270 personal working in the 14 Municipalities and the 9 ASD states and beyond project sites and a strong network established for information sharing and dissemination on land degradation and desertification issues and how to address them through SLM, SFM and FLR. 
Outcome 4.2: Policymakers and farmers, private sector and education stakeholders have capacity to implement SFM, FLR, INRM and biodiversity conservation.
The targeted project values for this outcome are increased production and use of education, extension and dissemination materials (3 videos, 48 radio spots, 9 events with family farmers, distribution of 5,000 booklets to educational institutions, new editions of 5 books and 10 technical or exchange events).
Outcome 5.1: Synergy with complementary initiatives to promote sustainable management and restoration benefits. 
Outcome 5.2: Project implemented with results-based management and application of findings/lessons learnt.

projects.name: UN WOMEN (UNFPA, UNHCR) 00129134 Refugee and migrant women in Brazil economically empowered
projects.description: UN Women efforts, as part of the joint programme Economic Empowerment of Refugee and Migrant Women in Brazil, funded by the Government of Luxembourg (implemented in partnership with the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR)), aims to ensure that policies and strategies of companies and public and private institutions strengthen economic rights and development opportunities for Venezuelan refugee and migrant women. To achieve this objective, the initiative is built on three axis. The first targets companies, institutions and governments on issues and actions related to decent work, social protection and entrepreneurship. The second directly addresses refugee and migrant women, so that they have access to training and opportunities to participate in decision-making processes related to the labor market and entrepreneurship. And the third also targets refugee and migrant women, so that they have knowledge and access to services that respond to gender-based violence.

projects.name: PAHO/WHO (MPTF Legal Amazon) Comprehensive protection and promotion of the rights of indigenous children, adolescents and young people in the Brazilian Amazon basin
projects.description:
OUTCOME 1: PROMOTING PUBLIC POLICIES TO REDUCE MATERNAL AND CHILD MORTALITY AND MALNUTRITION AMONG INDIGENOUS CHILDREN UNDER FIVE YEARS OLD.
Output 1.3: Local capacity strengthened to reduce Maternal and child morbidity and mortality, as well as malnutrition, in priority Special Indigenous Health Districts (DSEI), enhancing indigenous medicine and traditional midwifes activities, through a gender perspective and human rights based approach.

PAHO/WHO Activities:

1.3.1. Identify priority issues through prior community consultations and promote and implement intercultural dialogues to define strategies and culturally appropriate interventions to strengthen comprehensive health care for indigenous women, children, adolescents and young people in priority DSEIs, with gender lenses.

1.3.2. Produce guides and materials appropriate to the context of indigenous health for cultural adaptation and implementation of public policies to reduce maternal mortality in the indigenous territories of priority DSEIs, through gender lenses and knowledge dialogue workshops

1.3.3. Strengthen comprehensive health care for indigenous children, prioritizing the expansion and updating of the Integrated Strategy for the Prevention of Childhood Diseases (AIDPI), including an adapted methodology for indigenous health agents (community AIDPI) in priority DSEIs in alignment with activity 1.1.1.

1.3.4. Train health professionals and vaccinators at the Base Centers to work in a qualified manner in vaccination for the development of microplanning actions in high-quality vaccination activities; and in epidemiological surveillance and surveillance of events supposedly attributable to vaccination or immunization (ESAVI), in the context of the Regional Initiative for the Elimination of Diseases and Health Conditions 30+ and the sustainable development goals with a focus on Indigenous Base Centers and riverside populations in indigenous areas.

1.3.5. Strengthen the cold chain with high-quality equipment and supplies, pre-qualified by the WHO, ensuring efficiency in the conservation and transportation of vaccines and the safety of immunization actions in indigenous areas.

OUTCOME 2: EXPANDING ACCESS TO CONTRACEPTIVE METHODS AND SEXUAL AND REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH SERVICES FOR THE INDIGENOUS POPULATION.


Output 2.1: Four (4) Selected DSEIs in the Legal Amazon strengthened in the promotion of sexual and reproductive health and rights
Output 2.2: Priority DSEIs strengthened for health education, including the promotion of sexual and reproductive health with gender perspective and human rights-based approach.


PAHO/WHO:

2.2.1. Identify priority issues through prior community consultations and promote and implement intercultural dialogues to define strategies and culturally appropriate interventions for the promotion of sexual and reproductive health in priority DSEIs.

2.2.2. Train indigenous health professionals (multidisciplinary indigenous health teams and/or indigenous health workers) in the promotion of sexual and reproductive health, with gender, life-course and intercultural approach, in priority DSEIs.

OUTCOME 3: PROMOTING THE INTEGRAL DEVELOPMENT OF INDIGENOUS ADOLESCENTS AND YOUTH.
Output 3.3: Indigenous adolescents and youth mobilized for actions promoting indigenous health


PAHO/WHO Activities:

3.3.1. Identify priority issues through prior consultations with indigenous adolescents and youth in the communities, and promote and implement intercultural dialogues to define culturally appropriate strategies and interventions to increase social mobilization and participation in promoting indigenous health, including psychosocial care and practices related to alcohol and drug use, sexual and reproductive health.

3.3.2. Conduct workshops to raise awareness and mobilize Indigenous adolescents and youth for community-based actions on Indigenous health, including psychosocial care and practices related to alcohol and drug use, sexual and reproductive health.

OUTCOME 4: PROMOTING INCLUSIVE TERRITORIAL GOVERNANCE AND INDIGENOUS MULTILINGUAL EDUCATION.
Output 4.3: Strengthening the participation of indigenous medicine specialists, especially women, in territorial governance bodies and indigenous multilingual education

PAHO/WHO Activities:

4.3.1. Promote two meetings of indigenous medicine experts, especially indigenous women leaders, from priority DSEIs, in conjunction with indigenous movements and organizations, to encourage participation in territorial governance bodies.

4.3.2. Carry out community-based health education actions to strengthen ancestral practices and knowledge of indigenous medicine on priority topics to be defined in the territorial context.

OUTCOME 5: PREVENTING VIOLENCE AGAINST INDIGENOUS CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND YOUTH, INCLUDING REFUGEES AND MIGRANTS.
Output 5.3: Training and strengthening of strategies developed by the DSEIs in preventing sexual and gender-based violence against indigenous children, adolescents, and youth.

PAHO/WHO Activities:

5.3.1. Identify priority issues, based on prior consultation with indigenous adolescents and youth from the communities, and promote and implement intercultural dialogues to define culturally appropriate strategies and interventions for violence prevention.

5.3.2. Training of health workers who work in and with priority DSEIs in preventing sexual and gender-based violence against indigenous children, adolescents and youth.

5.3.3. Awareness-raising and mobilization workshops for indigenous adolescents and youth to carry out community-based actions on indigenous health.

projects.name: UNODC BRACF23 PEMS Authorities' capacities strengthened to address trafficking in persons for the purpose of forced labour in gold mining in the Tapajós River basin
projects.description:
Project: TAPAJÓS: A Prevalence-based Project to Reduce Forced Labor (Tapajós).
Actual start date: 01/10/2021.

This project aims to reduce the prevalence of forced labour in the gold mining sector in the State of Pará following evidence-based interventions to prevent trafficking in persons (TiP) and forced labour, protect victims and prosecute traffickers/explorers. Tapajós's Phase I was focused on producing knowledge on (a) the prevalence of TiP and forced labour, (b) the production chain of gold mining in the region, and (c) the convergence of crimes. The project's Phase II now targets applying evidence-based intervention to reach its goal. It is implemented under the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime's Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, especially Women and Children and the Protocol against the Smuggling of Migrants by Land, Sea and Air.
projects.outcome: 4.1.5 Capacidades governamentais fortalecidas para garantir uma abordagem multidimensional para combater crimes transnacionais, em especial durante crises humanitárias, e mitigar seus impactos sobre grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, compartilhando informações e aprimorando políticas orientadas por evidências, voltadas ao respeito aos direitos humanos e baseadas na igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia.

projects.name: UNEP Promoting integrated metropolitan planning and innovative urban technology investments in Brazil - CITinova II
projects.description:
The main challenge addressed by this project is that Brazilian metropolitan areas are growing unsustainably, based on an inefficient development model characterized by a high degree of urban sprawl, which has several negative consequences for the environment, including high levels of GHG emissions, significant loss of biodiversity, habitat fragmentation and increased pressures on ecosystem services. This model also makes urban governance costly and complex, and ultimately degrades quality of life in urban areas.
To address the aforementioned global environmental problems that Brazil is experiencing in an urban context, this project aims to accelerate the sustainable development of Brazilian metropolitan regions, Leading lo reductions in greenhouse gas emissions and the conservation of biodiversity. To this end, the project will increase local, state and federal capacity to undertake integrated urban planning, catalyze sustainable investments and facilitate long-term and sustainable urban development. Ultimately, the project aims to contribute toa sustainable transformation of the country's urban system and its development pattern.
To ensure the achievement of its objective, this project will focus on three distinct but representative metropolitan regions in Brazil, in addition to focusing on replicating and scaling-up good practices at the national level. The three pilot metropolitan regions are:
(1) Belém Metropolitan Region (RM Belém), located in the State of Pará in the northem and Amazonian region of the country;
(2) Greater Teresina Integrated Developmeot Region (Greater Teresina RIDE), in the northeast region in the states of Piauí and Maranhão. For most activities, the project will focus on the RIDE's ptimary urban area, the Timon-Teresina Urban Agglomeration; and,
(3) Florianópolis Metropolitan Region (RM Florianópolis), located in the State of Santa Catarina, in the southern region of the country.

projects.name: IFAD – 2000004380 – Payments for Ecosystem Sercivec promoted for deforestation-free supply chains in Brazil (CompensACTION Brazil)
projects.description:
The project "Promoting Payment for Environmental Services (PES) for deforestation-free production chains in Brazil" is part of a comprehensive set of activities called "CompensACTION for food security and a healthy planet", funded by Germany through the ASAP+. The other CompensACTION projects are currently integrated with ongoing loan-funded projects in Lesotho and Ethiopia. The CompensACTION initiative came into force on 15 November 2022 with the signing of the Supplementary Funds Agreement with Germany.

The project will address deforestation in Brazil, a problem that results in water scarcity, soil erosion and desertification, reduced air purification, loss of biodiversity and high carbon emissions. Consequently, ecosystem services are degraded. To combat these adverse effects, the project will pilot PES schemes based on deforestation-free production chains, with the aim of incentivising forest conservation and restoration. The pilot, which for Brazil will be called CompensAÇÃO, will be implemented by the Organização de Conservação da Terra (OCT), a competitively selected non-governmental organisation (NGO) that will operate the PES mechanism in the Cocoa Region of southern Bahia. The project aims to provide an incentive to promote the agroforestry transition of cocoa growing areas towards production arrangements that are less dependent on external inputs, towards more profitable and economically viable agroecological systems and with greater potential for providing ecosystem services, favouring increased production and income, and in turn providing mitigation of forest degradation and deforestation processes. CompensAÇÃO targets the poorest and most vulnerable people in Bahia's Atlantic Forest.

Actual Start Date: 04/04/2024
Actual End Date: 30/06/2028

Financial Information
Total cost: US$ 4.9 million
IFAD loan: US$ 4.4 million (ASAP+ through German Gov)
OCT counterpart: US$ 0.5 million

projects.name: UNODC GLOX99 GMCP Law enforcement agencies' capacities strengthened to address transnational organized crime and illicit trafficking through fluvial means in the Amazon basin and in the tri-border area between Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina
projects.description:
#SSC Colombia, Paraguay, Cape Verde, Guinea Bissau, Mozambique, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Tanzania.
Project: Global Maritime Crime Programme (GMCP).
Actual start date: 19/08/2022 | End date: End date: 30/09/2024.

GMCP assists Member States in enhancing and coordinating their efforts against maritime crime. In Brazil, GMCP has three fronts of action. The first aims to strengthen Brazil’s interagency capacity on river and maritime control and the country's prosecutorial capacity to disrupt organized crime in the Amazon basin, including cross-border cooperation with Northern neighbouring countries. The second focuses on the Southern Tri-Border of Brazil (with Paraguay and Argentina), aiming to equip law enforcement agencies and criminal justice sectors with skills to detect, interdict, investigate and prosecute threats in rivers, especially trafficking. Thirdly, GMCP promotes cooperation between Brazil and West African countries. GMCP is implemented under UNODC's mandate of the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and the Three International Drug Control Conventions.

Project: Center for Studies on Drug and Social Community Development (CDESC)

The former Center of Excellence on Illicit Drug Supply Reduction was remodeled into the Center for Studies on Drug and Social Community Development (CDESC) in 2024. CDESC aims to produce evidence and human rights-based studies and analyses on drug policy. It focuses on prevention, innovation, alternative development, human rights, and vulnerable populations.

The project is the result of a partnership between the National Secretariat for Drug Policy and Asset Management of the Ministry of Justice and Public Security (SENAD/MJSP), the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). It is implemented under UNODC's mandate on the Three International Drug Control Conventions.

projects.name: UNODC BRACF23 AURUM Law enforcement and environmental oversight agencies' capacities strenghened to reduce organized criminal activity related to illegal mining and trafficking of mercury in the Brazilian Amazon
projects.description:
Project: Combating Illegal Mining and Gold and Mercury Trafficking through Law Enforcement Cooperation in the Brazilian Amazon - Project Aurum.

The project aims to reduce organized criminal activity related to illegal mining and trafficking of mercury to promote the rule of law and economic development in the Brazilian Amazon. Its main outcomes include: 

(i) generating better understanding of the criminal networks involved in illegal mining and convergent crimes in the northern region of Brazil amongst law enforcement and the judiciary
(ii) improving operational structure and law enforcement authority response through alignment of internal procedures and regulations
(iii) enhance technical law enforcement capacity to prevent and combat illegal mining and mercury trafficking related to illegal mining
(iv) strengthened regional cooperation among law enforcement agencies through the fostering of effective intelligence sharing and coordinated strategies against illegal mining, and
(v) increased traceability of mercury to ensure follow-up investigations after seizures.

It is implemented under the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and in line with the Global Programme on Crimes that Affect the Environment.

projects.description: After a request from the Ministry of Environment of Brazil, CCAC will provide its support to the elaboration of the mitigation component of the Brazil 2024-2035 Climate Plan, with a higher climate ambition, a process which will inform the update of Brazil National Determined Contributions (NDC) for 2025 and prepare the country’s trajectory towards net zero emissions by 2050. As part of the mitigation component, to be supported both by CCAC and UNEP Copenhagen Climate Center, Brazil aims to elaborate sectoral mitigation plans to lay down the pathway to achieve the country’s climate commitment, particularly the integration of methane as a short-lived climate pollutant (SLCP), alongside other greenhouse gas (GHG). The project ensures methane reduction consideration is mainstreamed into overall's Climate Plan by looking integration across sectors and the co-benefits of measures for adaptation and other sustainable development goals. As a signatory of the Global Methane Pledge, Brazil committed to the global goal of 30% of methane reduction by 2030 and expressed interest to strengthen methane in its NDC revision aligned with country's climate change policy framework.

projects.name: UNEP Implementation of the Strategic Action Programme to ensure Integrated and Sustainable Management of the Transboundary Water Resources of the Amazon River Basin Considering Climate Variability and Change
projects.description:
The Project's overarching goal is to aid basin countries in implementing the Strategic Action Programme (SAP), fostering Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) in a source-to-sea continuum. This approach aims to deliver ecological, social, and economic benefits, supporting Amazon riparian countries in meeting sustainable development goals (SDGs) and convention targets. The Project operates through four key Components:
The Project is being executed through four Components:
Component 1 will strengthen the current national and regional institutional IWRM framework and develop a financial sustainability strategy to facilitate fund raising for SAP implementation, as well as ACTO’s role in conservation finance for improved IWRM. 
Components 2 will build community resilience to address the impacts of climate change in the Amazon Basin in order to reduce damages from extreme climactic events; ensure water security in the context of adaptation to climate change; and enhance resilience of coastal ecosystems. The component will also touch on the issues of infrastructure resilience in the context of climate change, promoting technical dialogue on infrastructure resilience and sustainability, facilitating exchange of best practices on risk analysis and environmental impact assessment and improving understanding of the Nexus and progress towards achievement of SDG9 in the Amazon basin. 
Component 3 will implement integrated environmental and water resources monitoring systems in order to establish basin wide compatible information to guide science-to-policy decision-making in IWRM and for conservation and protection of the bio-aquatic ecosystems. A supplement to the existing TDA/SAP and National Action Plans (NAP) using TWAP indicators will facilitate interconnections between national and regional activities, supporting national reports related to international conventions and SDGs. 
Component 4 provides project management tools, as well as a system to monitor SAP implementation over time. This component will also promote project visibility within the Amazon Basin and worldwide, facilitating ACTO’s positioning and recognition as an IWRM coordination agency for the Amazon Basin.
The Amazon Cooperation Treaty Organization (ACTO) is the Executing Agency for the Project. National government partners include: Ministries of Foreign Affairs in the 8 basin countries, Ministry of Environment and Water (Bolivia), National Water and Basic Sanitation Agency (Brazil), Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (Colombia), Ministry of Environment, Water and Ecological Transition (Ecuador), Ministry of Agriculture / Hydromet Service (Guyana), National Water Authority (Peru), Ministry of Spatial Planning and Environment (Suriname), and the People’s Power Ministry for Eco-socialism and the PP Ministry of Atention to Water (Venezuela).

projects.name: UNODC GLOZ83 CRIMJUST National actors' capacities strengthened to promote transnational investigations, criminal justice actions & cooperation, with a view of disrupting organised crime networks
projects.description:
#SSC Latin America and West Africa.
Project: Criminal Network Disruption Global Programme (CRIMJUST).

CRIMJUST aims contribute to the reduction of the impact of organised crime and related corruption on the security and rule of law of countries along illicit trafficking routes. In January 2023, a new third phase of CRIMJUST was launched to strengthen transnational investigations, criminal justice actions and criminal justice cooperation along illicit trafficking routes in Africa, Latin America, and the Caribbean. This phase focuses on identifying and disrupting organised crime groups and high-level criminal targets, via a three-tier intervention: (a) investigating and prosecuting transnational illicit trafficking, (b) depriving organized crime groups of illicit proceeds, and (c) fostering institutional integrity and promoting Human Rights Standards. CRIMJUST is implemented under UNODC's mandate of the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and the Three International Drug Control Conventions.

projects.name: IOM PX.0685 Aqui é Brasil Programme: Multisectoral strengthening of the Brazilian government's efforts for humanized reception, human rights protection, and reintegration of forcibly returned Brazilians
projects.description:
The project aims to ensure that forcibly returned Brazilians have access to comprehensive support and reception services upon arrival. Coordinated by IOM, in partnership with the Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship (MDHC)—as well as ther minitries and state and municipal governments, civil society, and the private sector, the initiative seeks to strengthen government protection mechanisms, facilitate socio-economic reintegration, and improve public actions for humanized reception.
The project is structured around four main pillars:
Humanized reception, protection, and emergency response at airports, ensuring immediate support and identification of specific needs.
Support for social and economic reintegration, including assistance for documentation, access to job opportunities, and support for family reunification.
Strengthening migration governance, to improve interministerial coordination, generate strategic data on the profile of returnees, and support evidence-based public policies.
Strategic partnerships and multisectoral cooperation, promoting integration among federal, state, and municipal governments, the private sector, and community organizations to ensure sustainable long-term solutions.

Actual start date: 01/03/2021.

This project aims to improve regional cooperation and capacity of enforcement and justice system actors to detect, interdict, investigate and prosecute transnational conservation crimes (TCCs) in the Amazon. To reach that, it focuses on (a) improving information exchange and regional cooperation between the Amazon countries, and (b) enhancing the capacity of enforcement and justice system actors to respond to TCCs. It is implemented under the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and in line with the Global Programme on Crimes that Affect the Environment.

#SSC Paraguay, Peru, Colombia.

This project focuses on addressing the work of Transnational Criminal Organizations (TCOs) in Brazil and bordering countries. To enable so, it divides itself into two main objectives: the first aim is to promote the use, in Brazil and Paraguay, of innovative practices to enhance prison management in line with international minimum standards, with a focus on the challenges posed by organized crime in prisons, promoting cooperation between both countries. Project: Strengthening Early Warning Systems and Responses to Environmental Crimes Related to Illegal Gold Mining in Indigenous Territories.

This project seeks to promote a model of preparedness and early warning to respond to risks and impacts caused by environmental crimes related to illegal gold mining in indigenous territories in the Amazon region. It builds upon the results of the evidence-based studies produced by UNODC under the Tapajós Project, implemented in the gold mining area of the Tapajós region in the State of Pará. projects.name: UNEP Transboundary cooperation for the conservation, sustainable development and integrated management of the Pantanal - Upper Paraguay River Basin
projects.description:
The project aims to promote water security through strengthening transboundary water governance, sustainable development, balancing multiple-use and promoting integrated management of the Pantanal-Upper Paraguay River Basin for the social and economic well-being of the population and for the conservation of the freshwater ecosystem, its services, its biodiversity and connectivity.
The project is structured into these components:
Strengthening cooperation for integrated river basin management (UNEP): This component focuses on enhancing collaboration to facilitate integrated management of the river basin.
Consolidating and sharing knowledge and developing a common understanding of the Pantanal-Upper Paraguay Basin: This component, led by both UNEP and IDB, aims to consolidate knowledge and establish a shared understanding of the basin.
Towards trinational planning for sustainable management of the basin: IDB and UNEP jointly lead this component, which works towards trinational planning to ensure the sustainable management of the basin.
On-the-ground interventions promoting integrated water resources management and sustainable finance: This component, led by both IDB and UNEP, involves practical interventions to promote integrated water resources management and sustainable finance.
Awareness building, stakeholder involvement: UNEP leads this component, focusing on raising awareness and involving stakeholders in the project's objectives and activities.

projects.description: The project aims to address land insecurity and gender inequality as critical factors that perpetuate cycles of poverty, social exclusion and environmental degradation in Maranhão. For that, the sustainable management of the land governance policy and the valorization and empowerment of rural women will be promoted through the following interventions: 1. Land and environmental regularization: Identification of the public to be benefited - women heads of household in rural communities, with priority given to family farming areas and traditional communities -, information gathering, awareness-raising and training work on documents needed for land and environmental regularization; 2.Training in sustainable practices: Development of workshops on agricultural management integrated with the bioeconomy, entrepreneurship and management of natural resources, with a focus on female participation, aimed at promoting access to rural credit and support for income generation 3. Strengthening institutional capacities to reduce deforestation: Integrating the actions of ITERMA, the Environment Secretariat (SEMA) and the Rural Research and Extension Agency (AGERP) to expand land governance, land-use planning and environmental monitoring, promoting an inclusive and sustainable approach.

The project aims to ensure that women paid care workers and women who undertake unpaid care work have access to decent work, as well as to promote a coresponsibility culture in society, to not overburden women with unpaid care work and, thus support their economic empowerment.

projects.name: UNODC BRACF23 Environmental UK Law enforcement agencies' and Indigenous peoples' capacities to investigate, denounce and disrupt illegal mining and related environmental crimes in the Brazilian Amazon
projects.description:
#SSC Peru, Ecuador
Project: Strengthening Financial lnvestigations, Regional Cooperation, and Community Resilience to Counter Environmental Crime in the Amazon

The project aims to enhance the capacity of law enforcement agencies in Brazil and Peru to investigate and disrupt illegal mining and related environmental crimes through targeted training, mentoring, and cross-border cooperation. By integrating institutional strengthening, regional intelligence sharing, and community-based support—especially in indigenous territories—the project will contribute to reducing illicit financial flows, improving environmental protection, and reinforcing the rule of law across the region.

projects.name: UNEP Development of impact investment mechanisms and solutions for sustainability goals (Amazon, Cerrado and Chaco)
projects.description: IFACC is an initiative of the the United Nations Environment Programme, The Nature Conservancy, and the Tropical Forest Alliance to significantly increase and accelerate lending and investment in sustainable agriculture in Brazil, Argentina and Paraguay. IFACC’s goal is to mobilize $10 billion in commitments and disbursements by 2030 by bringing together leading companies, banks and investors who work together to meet the need for transitional finance in the production of beef, soy, and other agricultural products without further deforestation or conversion. By the end of 2022, IFACC had $4.3 billion in commitments and disbursed $111 million.

projects.name: UNODC GLOZ31 CRIMFLO Law enforcement and criminal justice system actors' capacities strengthened to detect and prevent timber trafficking
projects.description:
Project: Strengthening the criminal justice system response to illegal deforestation and timber trafficking – from crime scene to court (CRIMFLO).
Actual start date: 26/09/2022.

This project has three main objectives: (a) improved inter-agency cooperation at the state and federal levels, (b) enhanced capacity and knowledge for front-line officers, and (c) increased private-sector cooperation. It focuses on 1) enhancing capacities of investigators, prosecutors, and judiciary to effectively handle a crime scene and case management, ensuring an effective process from crime scene to court, and 2) providing training and capacity building activities for front-line officers on trade supply chain security, law enforcement and customs training to detect and prevent timber trafficking. It is implemented under the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and in line with the Global Programme on Crimes that Affect the Environment.

projects.name: UNESCO 914BRZ4029 Democracy promoted in Brazil through heritage and memory
projects.description: The International Technical Cooperation Project between UNESCO and the Federal Supreme Court (STF) of Brazil aims at the physical expansion, the development of the new exhibition project and the curatorial management of the Minister Sepúlveda Pertence Museum, of the Federal Supreme Court (“STF Museum” ), with the purpose of promoting democratic values, human rights, constitutional culture and citizenship in Brazil. The partnership between UNESCO and the STF will transform the STF Museum into a reference cultural center for the promotion of memory and education for democracy, with the general aim of safeguarding and disseminating the history of Brazilian constitutionalism, the achievement of fundamental and human rights and the creation of the Federal Supreme Court itself. This project aims to bring the Court closer to society and expand understanding of the importance of the Constitution and the STF for the protection of rights and the democratic regime.

projects.name: UNEP Develop a Vehicle Emissions Inspection Programme
projects.description: The project supports Brazil's Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MMA) in reducing short-lived climate pollutants (black carbon, PM 2.5, and sources of tropospheric ozone) from road vehicles through two complementary workstreams. The International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT) leads the development of national vehicle inspection guidelines, state-of-the-art analysis of inspection technologies, and a practical guide for subnational governments to implement heavy-duty vehicle inspection programmes, alongside engagement with potential financiers for a pilot project. The Institute of Energy and Environment (IEMA) leads the update of Brazil's road emissions inventory (last produced in 2013) and the development of a web-based platform for automatic emissions calculations and data dissemination, enabling both federal and state governments to monitor and act on vehicle emission data.

projects.name: UNESCO 914BRZ1159 Basic Education strengthened in Brazil
projects.description: This project focuses on contributing to the strengthening of programs implemented by Basic Education Secretariat of the Brazilian Ministry of Education (SEB-MEC) aimed at improving the quality of basic education in all its stages, considering the specificities of the various audiences and teaching modalities, access, permanence, learning, and equity. In this context, the project intends to provide technical inputs for the improvement of national educational public policies aimed at enhancing the quality of learning and the appreciation and qualification of teachers, ensuring equal conditions for access and permanence in basic education in line with the full development of the person, the exercise of citizenship, and preparation for the world of work. Among the planned activities are: conducting diagnostics to support the formulation of guidelines, protocols, and directives for basic education, mapping and disseminating good pedagogical practices within the scope of basic education curricula, developing innovative educational methodologies for the training of education professionals, supporting the conception of monitoring and evaluation strategies, and developing materials for technical improvement within the scope of SEB/MEC’s priority programs.

projects.name: UNEP Strengthening the national transparency system in Brazil under the Paris Agreement (DataClima+)
projects.description: This Capacity Building Initiative for Transparency (CBIT) project aims to strengthen Brazil's climate transparency system to meet the ETF requirements under the Paris Agreement. Through DataClima+, Brazil will formalize and streamline the governance of climate data required to comply with ETF requirements and to inform decision-making, thus addressing Measurement, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) challenges reported in previous National Communications.  To produce high-quality climate information, the country will improve and optimize its climate data management cycle, including as related to planning, data collection, data processing and analysis, information publishing and sharing, data preservation, and data reuse. Thus, the project will develop and implement policies, rules, processes, organizational structures, and technologies following the best practices of governance and business process management, with standardized, well-documented procedures that serve as the basis of the organizational knowledge management approach, increasing the system’s efficiency and, more importantly, MCTI’s productivity in preparing subsequent transparency reports. Moreover, the project will implement the institutional arrangements required for the timely reception of raw data and provide the capacity building required to ensure that key stakeholders benefit from the newly developed information system.

This project addresses three key issues:

- Ensuring that a successful approach to employment training for groups vulnerable to discrimination on grounds sensitive to gender and covered by international labour and human rights standards is adapted and more widely available both in terms of potential trainees and in occupations covered.

projects.name: UNHCR (MPTF SD of Brazilian Legal Amazon) builds institutional and community resilience through health, education, anti-xenophobia training, livelihoods, and climate initiatives, fostering rights, inclusion, and peaceful coexistence for indigenous refugees and migrants
projects.description: Sub-output exclusive to MPTF for the Sustainable Development of the Brazilian Legal Amazon). UNHCR strengthens institutional and community capacities to respond to humanitarian crises and promote socio-economic integration of indigenous refugees and migrants. Activities include reinforcing the indigenous health promoters project and organizing workshops for health professionals on culturally sensitive approaches in urban contexts. UNHCR supports the creation of educational spaces and Portuguese language courses tailored to indigenous communities, alongside literacy programs and youth and adult education initiatives adapted to their cultural specificities. The organization also advances socio-environmental innovation through the establishment of Sustainability Centers, which promote environmental education, traditional knowledge, and productive inclusion linked to the Amazon bioeconomy. To combat racism and xenophobia, UNHCR organizes intersectoral training sessions for local protection networks, involving actors from health, education, justice, and security sectors. Furthermore, UNHCR implements livelihood strengthening programs that combine training in handicrafts, agroecology, entrepreneurship, and digital skills with mentoring in financial management and market access. These efforts are complemented by support for refugee-led organizations through public calls for proposals, fostering community bonds and peaceful coexistence. Finally, UNHCR facilitates indigenous participation in climate-related events such as the Climate Mural pre-COP activity, ensuring their voices are included in global discussions on sustainability.

projects.description: The decline in fertility rates in Brazil in the last decade has had profound implications upon the demographic trend of its pyramid with a clear trend towards a growing elderly population. projects.name: WHO/ PAHO Country Envelope
projects.description:
Output 1 - HIV Prevention: Consolidate the expansion of equitable services in combination prevention, including in Primary Care Services, for key populations and groups at high risk of HIV (particularly LGBTI, indigenous peoples, persons deprived of liberty, persons living in street, migrants and refugees) in a national scale. Support the local governments to ensure equitable access to services in combination prevention, treatment, care and support to persons living with, at risk of and affected by HIV, with focus on PrEP and HIV self-testing among LGBTI people, sex workers, persons deprived of liberty, indigenous peoples, persons living in street, migrants and refugees. Foster the use of inequalities lens and the focus on gender equality to the HIV response, strengthening community-led initiatives.  Strengthen local community capacities and community based activities on HIV combination prevention taylored for and with key population. Foster leadership of women living with HIV/Aids and support community based activities with focus on closing service gaps among women in vulnerable situation, particularly migrants and refugees, deprived of liberty, living in streets and indigenous peoples.			

Output 2 - HIV Treatment: Scale up HIV testing, treatment, care, support and integrated people-centred services, particularly in Brazilian border area and with emphasis on addressing structural drivers of inequalities to improve equitable access to services. Strengthen integrated services, particularly with Primary Health Care, in prioritized regions. Foster leadership of women living with HIV/Aids and support community based activities with focus on closing service gaps among key population, particularly migrants and refugees, deprived of liberty, living in streets and indigenous peoples. Support local governments to expand HIV integrated services, particularly to timely response to advanced HIV disease/AIDS treatment, care and support in north border area, considering inequalities. Strengthen equitable integrated services, particularly to reduce HIV/Aids morality and mortality rate, to adopt innovative strategies to prevent interruption of treatment, as well as to expand HIV-TB treatment, HIV/STI/HV services.			

Output 3 - Pediatric AIDS and Vertical Transmission: Strengthen and consolidate EMTCT Plus initiative in Brazil, particularly in north region tackling inequalities to ensure equitable access to services in prevention, treatment, care and support. Strengthening gender equality perspective in local investigation committees to the elimination of HIV vertical transmission. Foster leadership of women living with HIV/Aids and support community based activities with focus on closing service gaps among women in vulnerable situation, particularly migrants and refugees, deprived of liberty, living in streets and indigenous peoples. Support the implementation of the National strategy for the elimination of HIV/Syphilis/VH vertical transmission in priority cities, ensuring that the needs and priorities of women and girls, in all their diversities, affected by and living with HIV are prioritized.

projects.name: UNESCO 914BRZ3054 Governance and compliance of the State of Goiás improved based on ethical standards
projects.description: This Project aims to create the necessary conditions for the process of implementation and dissemination of the principles of compliance and integrity in the context of the Public Administration of the State of Goiás. With the leading role and leadership of the State Comptroller General – body of internal control linked directly to the state Executive Branch, the project intends to leverage the State of Goiás as a reference in the adoption of procedures to improve its governance instruments, transparency and efficiency in decision-making by part of public power. To this end, UNESCO aims to build a normative framework based on the following axes: 1) Ethics and Accountability; 2) Transparency; 3) Governance and Risk Management; and 4) Citizen Participation. In this way, a series of good practices shall be developed, with the potential to be raised to the level of reference and guiding compass for replicability and application in other contexts of local governments that seek to improve their decision-making processes, the structuring of mechanisms of governance and bringing citizens closer to public authorities.

projects.name: UN WOMEN 02000941/00130001 Private sector companies have enhanced capacity to promote social norms
projects.description:
Private sector companies have enhanced capacity to promote social norms through their participation in the Unstereotype Alliance. The UA is a thought and action platform that uses advertising as a force for good to drive positive change. It seeks to eradicate harmful gender-based stereotypes. The alliance is focused on empowering women in all their diversity (race, class, age, ability, ethnicity, religion, sexuality, language, education, etc.) and addressing harmful masculinities to help create a gender equal world. The Alliance brings together a powerful growing global coalition of leading industry players behind the common goal of eliminating gender bias and harmful gender stereotypes from their advertising.

The program focuses on three key strategic priorities:  

Fostering an unstereotyped culture within the business environment, with an emphasis on diversity and inclusionary practices.  

Developing principles and guidelines for businesses to adhere to in order to create progressive portrayals in advertising content that is free from stereotypes  

Driving social change through communications that raise awareness of stereotypes among the public, and to encourage action to end stereotypes and end discrimination.

projects.name: UNHCR (MPTF SD of Brazilian Legal Amazon) strengthens access to documentation and culturally sensitive services for indigenous refugees and migrants, enabling rights, protection, and inclusion through legal assistance, training, and community-based initiatives
projects.description: Sub-output exclusive to MPTF for the Sustainable Development of the Brazilian Legal Amazon). UNHCR works to guarantee the rights and legal identity of indigenous refugees and migrants by promoting access to documentation and culturally sensitive protection services. This includes organizing regular documentation task forces in Pacaraima to issue essential civil documents such as identity cards, birth certificates, and work permits, as well as supporting naturalization processes for indigenous communities affected by displacement. To ensure these services are accessible and culturally appropriate, UNHCR hires indigenous cultural mediators and trains community volunteers to assist in documentation efforts both inside and outside shelters. Complementing these actions, UNHCR conducts workshops and training sessions for local protection networks and shelter teams, in partnership with institutions such as FUNAI, to strengthen their capacity to provide culturally sensitive assistance and uphold the rights of indigenous refugees and migrants.

projects.name: UNESCO 570BRZ2050 Reforestation programmes supported in the biosphere reserve of Mata Atlantica
projects.description: This four-year project covers an area comprised by three Brazilian states (Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo and Espirito Santo), a highly populated territory marked by a rich biodiversity and important natural and cultural assets of the Brazilian heritage. The area is home to the Brazilian Biosphere of Mata Atlantica and has also an intense connection with the Ocean with large ports and oil industries based in the region, important fishery centers, pristine islands and other well-protected forest and marine ecosystems. As todays’ “economic center” of Brazil, with large urban centers advancing over the Mata Atlantica biome, the region is also marked by successful cases of conservation programmes allying economic development to environmental programmes. It is indeed one of the few areas of Brazil where original large forests of Mata Atlantica remain untouched, this thanks to governmental laws and a combined effort of local NGOs involved in the preservation of the unique characteristics of the region. The project is therefore indeed to explore existing synergies with a qualified network of local partners (UNESCO biosphere reserves, UNESCO chairs, well-known NGOs with large presence in the territory etc) to mitigate the negative effects of an old development paradigm. The project will enable sustainable education programmes, reforestation activities and other science-based strategies (carbon sequestration, blue economy etc) as viable alternatives to local inhabitants.

projects.name: UNHCR (MPTF SD of Brazilian Legal Amazon) fosters peaceful coexistence through intercultural dialogue, indigenous women’s participation, and livelihood initiatives, supporting a national strategy for indigenous refugees and migrants aligned with human rights and social inclusion
projects.description: Sub-output exclusive to MPTF for the Sustainable Development of the Brazilian Legal Amazon). UNHCR promotes peaceful coexistence and social inclusion through a series of intercultural initiatives that bring together indigenous refugees, migrants, and host communities. These activities include organizing cultural events and awareness campaigns to reduce discrimination and address gender-based violence, ensuring the participation of girls, young women, and LGBTIQ+ individuals. UNHCR also supports indigenous women’s engagement in national advocacy spaces, such as the Indigenous Women’s March, amplifying their voices in policy discussions. In partnership with the Ministry of Indigenous Peoples, UNHCR provides technical assistance for the development of a National Strategy for Indigenous Refugees and Migrants, facilitating consultations and hiring specialized consultants to ensure a participatory process. Additionally, UNHCR fosters economic inclusion and cultural visibility through handicraft initiatives that showcase indigenous knowledge and craftsmanship during global events like COP 30.

projects.name: IOM PX.0543 Improving Reintegration Outcomes for Survivors of Modern Slavery
projects.description: The project’s overall objective is to improve voluntary return and reintegration outcomes for survivors of modern slavery. IOM’s intervention aims to enhance the UK’s capacity to improve return outcomes through three key outputs. First, a comprehensive assessment of current voluntary return arrangements for survivors of all genders and ages in the UK will be conducted. Second, a national mapping of available reintegration services and access in common countries of return will be completed. Finally, voluntary return support providers across the UK will gain enhanced capacity to conduct risk assessments and develop risk management plans, ensuring consistency in the referral process.

projects.name: IOM PX.0650 Improving Reintegration Outcomes for Survivors of Modern Slavery (Phase 2)
projects.description: This project seeks to address these gaps by enhancing the capacities of key actors to improve voluntary return and reintegration processes and outcomes for survivors of modern slavery and human trafficking. Building on activities conducted in the first phase of the project (PX.0543), it will strengthen the understanding and capacity of key actors in the UK and in countries of return, such as Brazil. This will be done by assessing the role of police and local authorities in the voluntary return of survivors from the UK, as well as by building the capacity of key actors involved in voluntary return and reintegration and conducting or updating national mappings of available reintegration services in countries of return. Second, the project will enhance the engagement of survivors of modern slavery and human trafficking in the process of voluntary return and reintegration, to centre survivor voice and agency, by conducting lived experience research to understand the experiences of survivors who have returned, and by piloting a Virtual Orientation programme for survivors considering return from the UK, promoting survivor agency in decision making.

projects.name: UNDRR - City-to-city cooperation for climate and disaster resilience fostered via the mentorship of the Resilience Hubs of the "Making Cities Resilient 2030" initiative
projects.description:
MCR2030 Resilience Hubs are cities that demonstrate excellence and leadership in areas of disaster risk reduction, resilience and climate change adaptation. Interested cities can apply to the title of MCR2030 Resilience Hub by signing with UNDRR a Joint Work Plan that aims to mentor nearby local governments seeking support in the local level implementation of the Sendai Framework. 

In 2023, Salvador (BA), Porto Alegre (RS), and Barcarena (PA) have successfully applied to the title and joined Campinas (SP) and Recife (PE) as MCR2030 Resilience Hubs in Brazil. In 2024, the five Brazilian Hubs will support at least 3 municipalities in Brazil with a series mentorship actions, including: city-to-city knowledge exchange; capacity building support to other local governments; mentoring for project planning, strengthening of metropolitan governance for DRR. Those activities will be implemented with the normative guidance and technical support of UNDRR.
projects.outcome: 5.1.4 Capacidades fortalecidas dos governos, sociedade civil e organizações humanitárias para o desenvolvimento de políticas públicas e de estratégias de redução de riscos e gestão de desastres, baseadas em evidências e centradas no respeito aos direitos humanos e na igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia.

projects.name: FAO GCP /BRA/11052 P/GFF Atlantic Forest conservation supported through sustainable management of cocoa agroforestry landscapes
projects.description:
The Project “Conservation of the Atlantic Forest through the sustainable management of cocoa agroforestry landscapes” seeks to reduce and reverse the trends of degradation and biodiversity loss in Southern Bahia State by strengthening the cabruca cocoa production systems. This will be done through helping conservation and restoration of environmental services in rainforest formations in Southern Bahia through improved management of natural resources and strengthening of the cabruca cocoa value chain. 
The Project was endorsed by the GEF CEO in November 2022. The GEF approved USD 150,000 project preparation grant to support the project preparation phase. Activities during this phase will support the collection of key baseline information and the realization of stakeholder consultation, tasks needed for the documentation required for submission to approval by the GEF’s Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and FAO.

projects.name: OHCHR - UN Free & Equal Campaign being implented in Brazil
projects.description: The UN Free & Equal Campaign (UNFE) is being implemented in Brazil since 2014, under OHCHR leadership. The main goal of UNFE is to promote and protect the human right of LGBTQIA+ people, mainly through communication and awareness raising. In Brazil the implementation was expanded also to include other activities to build capacities of civil society organizations and LGBTQIA+ human rights defenders. The National UN Free & Equal Campaign in Brazil reflects the national context, having a special focus on specially vulnerable populations: trans people. This does not jeopardize the engagement and colaboration with other groups such as lesbian women, gay men, bissexual people, intersex people, and others. UNFE in Brazil has cooperated repeatedly with important stakeholders, among CSOs, governmental bodies, business, social media platforms, journalists, among others.

projects.name: UN WOMEN 02000663 Women have enhanced capacity to promote social norms and to prevent and respond to multiple forms of discrimination and violence
projects.description:
UN Women will prioritize innovative methodologies and strategies to address structural inequalities, systemic oppression, patriarchal and racist social norms exacerbated by political polarization, COVID-19, socioeconomic crisis, impacts of climate change and conflicts as the key root causes of violence against women and girls, especially women human rights defenders. Promoting positive social norms, the CO will focus on addressing the causes of social exclusion and compounded discrimination, which prevent different groups of women and girls from living a life free from violence and fully realising their human rights due to their gender, race, and ethnicity, among others.  

The CO will implement multi-dimensional interventions to achieve gender transformative results through social mobilization and advocacy, integrated normative and policy advice, building capacity for the implementation of state obligations on women’s human rights. The CO will implement innovative partnership strategies and advocacy campaigns in favour of positive social norms; provide integrated normative support to design/review, enforcement and monitoring of laws and strategies to prevent and respond to multiple forms of discrimination and violence; and facilitate increased access to and availability of quality multi-sectoral services for survivors, particularly in rural and forest settings. The CO will enhance institutional capacities of women human rights defenders’ organizations, especially grassroots women's groups of indigenous, Afro-descendant and quilombola, youth, LGBTQI+, and environmental activists strengthening their agency, voice, and meaningful engagement with human rights mechanisms and the UN Treaty Bodies. In prevention and response solutions, UN Women will mobilize individuals – including men and boys – and communities for effective whole community interventions; and establish multi-stakeholder platforms with federal and subnational governments, private sector companies, media, creative industry, and the sports ecosystem for joint action to address negative social norms and attitudes. The CO will promote UN-integrated and coordinated action as a co-chair of the UNSDCF Result Group on Social Inclusion, chair of the IATG-GRE, lead agency of the United Nations Secretary General (UNSG) UNiTE campaign to End Violence against Women and of the implementation of the UNCT SWAP on Gender and Race Equality Action Plan.

projects.description: OHCHR has a 4-point agenda on transformative change towards racial justice and equality, which sets a series of measures to be implemented by countries to actively combat racism and promote racial justice and equality. Also, OHCHR actively supports the activities of universal human rights mechanisms that address issues relating to racism – such as CERD, EMLER, SR on Racism, and others – and of the Permanent Forum on People of African Descent (PFPAD). To promote and implement such agenda and reflects such global efforts in Brazil, OHCHR aims at disseminating relevant content on relevant international human rights standards; guidance on promoting and ensuring the meaningful participation of people of African descent; technical assistance for policies and measures for a data-driven and human rights-based approach on combatting systemic racism and promoting racial justice; empowering and strengthening  CSOs and Human Rights Defenders of African descent to advocacy and defend their human rights; promote intersectionality and raise awareness on the complex, persistent and multiple challenges and human rights violations faced by people of African descent, as well as their concerns and proposals for transformative change.

projects.name: OHCHR – Indigenous and Quilombolas Fellowship Programme being implemented in Portuguese in Brazil
projects.description: The Indigenous Fellowship Programme is a OHCHR Uproject focused on strengthening the capacities and knowledge of Indigenous People to defend, participate and advocacy with the Universal Human Rights System. The Programme had a very small participation of Indigenous People from Brazil and other Portuguese-speaking countries, while these countries presented alarming scenarios of violence and human rights violations against Indigenous People and other Traditional Communities. Considering such context, in 2023 OHCHR launched a pilot programme in Brazil for an Indigenous Fellowship Programme in Portuguese – it was expanded for Quilombola to adequately reflect the national human rights context. The Indigenous and Quilombolas Fellowship Programme is developed under OHCHR leadership, in partnership with UN Agencies and national stakeholders among public bodies, universities and CSOs. Participants are involved in a preparatory phase implemented in Brasília, before travelling to Genebra to participate in human rights training and in session from human rights mechanisms. The Programme can be considered a successful initiative and it is being expanded to expand its impact, potential and results.

projects.name: OHCHR The right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment being protected in Brazil through a strengthened regional approach
projects.description: The Project Strengthening the regional approach for the protection of specific human rights concerns in the Latin America and the Caribbean has 3 main pillars: 1. Promoting the expansion of civic space and the protection of human rights defenders in the LAC Region, 2. Promoting and protecting the human rights of migrants in vulnerable situations, and 3. Promoting the right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment. It has a regional implementation for countries in Latin America and the Caribbean, being coordinated and implemented jointly by ROCA, ROSA and UN Human Rights Offices and Field Presences. In Brazil, the main focus in on the 3rd pillar, on the right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment. The implementation focus on increasing capacities to promote and support a rights-based environmental action; mainstreaming a human rights based approach to climate and environmental issues; contribute with local human rights based environmental actions and initiatives; promote participation, protection, access to justice and access to information for Environmental Human Rights Defenders (EHRD), Indigenous People, Quilombolas and other Traditional Communities; and strengthen partnerships with national stakeholders. Main activities include technical inputs to legislations and policies; promote the dialogue and exchange of good practices on participation of Indigenous People, women, children and people with disabilities in decision-making; organize and promote forums and regional encounters for EHRD; disseminating information on regional meetings regarding environmental and climate change issues; among others.

projects.name: UNAIDS (OHCHR) Civil society and the public sector strengthened to propose and monitor protective human rights laws
projects.description:
Considering that strengthening human rights is fundamental to addressing inequalities and, therefore, promoting a more effective response to HIV/AIDS in the most marginalized populations, the main objective of the project is to ensure that the populations most affected by the epidemic have greater protection of their civil and political rights through the implementation of protective public policies at the federal and local levels, contributing to the reduction of inequalities and a better response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic.
The project was born from a demand from the federal government to strengthen the debate on human rights in different areas and the analysis of global political movements by the UN system.
Given the global movement of anti-democratic legislation and against human rights, measuring the progress and regression of laws that make key populations vulnerable goes hand in hand with monitoring a political spectrum of interest for progressive agendas.
To date, the project will cover the following axes:
· Training in responsible advocacy for civil society
· Training rounds on strengthening human rights from legislative missions
· Formulation, creation and launch of the supporting document for the protection of human rights in the legislature
· Situation room for monitoring trends in the legislature and on social media

projects.name: UNEP Engaging with banks towards developing the Net Zero Banking Alliance
projects.description:
UNEPFI is a global network of 500 banks, insurers and investors. The mains objectives of UNEPFI are to Catalysing action across the financial system to align economies with sustainable development; Provide guidance to support banks, insurers and investors limit greenhouse gas emissions, protect nature, promote a circular economy and support financial inclusion; and Engage policymakers to help the development of effective financial regulation. 
In Latin America we have a membership of over 60 financial institutions, with 6 member banks in Brazil and 11 insurance Companies.  
We work with these members on activities that provide guidance on the implementation of the Principles for Responsible Banking, the Net Zero Banking Alliance, and the Principles for Sustainable Insurance. 
Moreover, we have seven supporting institutions to help catalyze action in the region. Among them, we have ongoing projects with FEBRABAN, the Brazilian Federation of Banks, and CNSEG, Brazilian Insurers Association.  We also provide support to the ongoing IFACC project that UNEP Climate Finance Unit coordinates. "

projects.name: UNIDO 210039 Industrial Deep Decarbonization Iniciative - IDDI
projects.description: O IDDI é a maior e mais diversificada coligação de governos e organizações do sector privado que trabalha para descarbonizar as indústrias pesadas, começando pelo aço, cimento e concreto. Ele trabalha com os governos para descarbonizar a indústria pesada, aumentando o mercado de aço, cimento e concreto com baixo teor de carbono e quase zero. Isto trará uma contribuição significativa para reverter as tendencias de alterações climáticas. Fazer aço, cimento e concreto com níveis baixos e próximos de zero requer que processos de produção inteiros sejam transformados, assim como inovação, investimento e alinhamento significativos. Para tal, são necessários dados robustos, normas para produtos com baixo e quase zero carbono e uma procura substancial, com uso de novas tecnologias e a crescente vontade política e industrial.

projects.name: UNIDO 220201 Accelerate-to-Demonstrate (A2D) Facility
projects.description: The Accelerate-to-Demonstrate (A2D) Facility aims to accelerate the commercialization of innovative clean energy technologies in developing countries. The A2D Facility will include support to innovators, research institutions and related organizations in the thematic areas of: critical minerals, clean hydrogen, smart energy and industrial decarbonization. The programme is funded through GBP 65 million from the UK Government’s Department for Energy Security & Net Zero (DESNZ), which includes the 1% UN coordination levy. It currently runs from 1st April 2023 to 31st March 2029. The programme’s main Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)-of-focus are SDGs 13 (climate action), 1 (no poverty) and 9 (industry, innovation and infrastructure), as well as contributing to a range of co-benefits, including, but not limited to, applying the principles of Leave No One Behind, a human rights-based approach, and gender equality and the empowerment of women that encapsulate the universal values on which the 2030 Agenda is based.
